newsitem.title: DUBAI: Dubai gold trade hopes for Indian wedding demand.
newsitem.headline: Dubai gold trade hopes for Indian wedding demand.

text.p: Dubai gold traders said on Sunday they were hoping that India's upcoming wedding season will make amends for disappointing jewellery and bullion sales during last week's Diwali (Festival of Light) holiday.

The second Indian marriage season, which runs from the middle of November to the end of February, usually sees a strong upturn in bullion and jewellery purchases, much of which is supplied from Dubai where prices are lower than in Bombay.
"We have to look now at the wedding buying," one Dubai souk (market) trader said.

Bullion imports into Dubai during this year's first Indian marriage season surged from 27.4 tonnes in March to 32.6 tonnes in April and 33.3 tonnes in May, the highest monthly import figures so far this year.
The Bombay Bullion Association estimates the number of Indian marriages at 10 million a year, with an average of 30 grams of gold bought for each wedding.
It is wedding and festival demand that makes India the world's single largest consumer on gold and Dubai a major re-exporter of the yellow metal.

Expectations of strong Indian demand have also been fanned by fiscal reforms implemented by the Indian central bank and expectations of a good harvest after strong monsoon rains between June and September.
An indicator of Diwali's effect on bullion imports into Dubai should emerge with the release of October import figures later this week by the World Gold Council in Dubai.
Dubai jewellers said that Diwali retail business in the main 22 carat jewellery sector was down up to 15 percent from last year's levels but that bullion re-export demand into India remained upbeat.
Imports in September this year ran to 26.58 tonnes, down from 28.84 tonnes in August and 29.89 tonnes in July, according to figures compiled by Dubai customs.
"It should be a turnaround month. Prices were attractive... India was buying more for the festivals," one souk trader said.
Dubai's benchmark Ten Tola (TT) bar -- 3.746 ounces of 24 carat gold -- was quoted by Dubai traders on Sunday at 5,255 UAE dirhams ($1,431.10), up from 5,245 dirhams on November 10.
Ten gram gold pieces were two dirhams higher at 450.
International spot bullion was last quoted on Saturday at $380.00-$380.50 an ounce, up from the London Friday fix of $379.50-$380.00 an ounce. ($1=3.672 UAE dirhams)
